title: Grateful Dead Live at Denver Coliseum on 1973-11-20

ai_review.summary: An extraordinary 1973 Denver second‑set with soaring Truckin', The Other One and Stella Blue jams, captured in a clean matrix mix that balances board clarity with audience ambience.
ai_review.review: The set is hailed as one of the band’s peak ’73 performances – “intensely tight”, “mind‑blowing” and full of high‑energy improvisations such as the Truckin' → The Other One sequence, the Mind Left Body jam and a soaring Stella Blue.  Listeners note that the matrix source provides a pleasant blend of a clean soundboard core with just enough audience presence to retain the live vibe, though there is a brief patch in the MLB section and occasional mids‑range dullness.  Overall the musical delivery outweighs the minor sonic quirks, making this recording a must‑listen for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently enthusiastic reviews praise the show’s energy and standout jams; most comments on the matrix source describe it as clear with only minor flaws, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: A well‑balanced matrix: clean soundboard foundation with modest audience ambience.  Reviewers mention crisp mids but note a slight dullness in highs/low end and a short patch during the Mind Left Body jam; overall the mix is pleasant and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Intense post‑lyric Truckin' jamming flows into a long, jazzy The Other One sequence with a dramatic mel­tdown jam, followed by the ethereal Mind Left Body and a beautiful, weeping Stella Blue finale.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his soaring guitar tone, especially on Stella Blue and the extended jams; described as “intensely tight” and “far‑out”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for powerful bass ‘bombs’ during Truckin' and his inventive lines in The Other One; several reviewers call his playing a standout.
